description: Two-panel composite figure giving the true stress–true strain and strain-hardening response of a Fe-22wt.% Mn-0.6wt.% C model TWIP steel at seven temperatures. (a) plots True Stress (GPa, y axis 0–1.4) against True Strain (x axis 0–0.5); (b) plots Hardening (GPa, y axis 0–5) against the same True Strain axis (0–0.5). Each of the seven temperatures — 293K, 373K, 473K, 573K, 673K, 773K, 873K — appears twice in the legends, once as a coloured solid line labelled "Simulation" and once as x-markers of the same colour labelled "Experiment"; the colour order from 293K to 873K is red, orange, light green, green, cyan, blue, purple. In (a) the simulated and experimental flow curves nearly coincide at 293–573K and separate slightly at 673K, 773K and 873K; flow stress decreases monotonically with rising temperature, the 293K curve approaching 1.4 GPa by strain 0.5 while the 873K curve flattens near 0.45 GPa. In (b) hardening starts near 3.5 GPa at low strain, the 293K curve showing a hump near strain 0.2–0.25 (about 2.5–2.7 GPa), whereas higher-temperature curves decay faster, the 873K curve falling near zero by strain ~0.4. Together the panels show that one coherent parameter set reproduces both the flow and the strain-hardening behaviour over the whole temperature range.

subfigures.description: True stress–true strain compression curves, True Stress (GPa) vs True Strain (0–0.5), for seven temperatures (293K, 373K, 473K, 573K, 673K, 773K, 873K); each temperature is given as a solid simulated line and same-coloured x-markers for experiment. Curves fall systematically with increasing temperature; the 293K pair rises to just below 1.4 GPa at strain 0.5 and the 873K pair flattens near 0.45 GPa. Simulation and experiment agree closely at 293–573K and deviate slightly at 673K, 773K and 873K.

Strain-hardening curves, Hardening (GPa, 0–5) vs True Strain (0–0.5), for the same seven temperatures with the same colour coding and Simulation/Experiment legend entries. All curves start near 3.0–3.6 GPa at low strain; the 293K simulation curve shows a local maximum (hump) near strain 0.2–0.25 at roughly 2.5 GPa with red experimental markers reaching about 2.7 GPa, while the higher-temperature curves decay monotonically and the 873K curve drops close to zero by strain ~0.4.

observations.observation: Panel (a) has x-axis 'True Strain' spanning 0 to 0.5 and y-axis 'True Stress (GPa)' spanning 0 to 1.4.
Panel (b) has x-axis 'True Strain' spanning 0 to 0.5 and y-axis 'Hardening (GPa)' spanning 0 to 5.

Both legends list seven temperatures - 293K, 373K, 473K, 573K, 673K, 773K and 873K - each with a 'Simulation' entry (solid coloured line) and an 'Experiment' entry (cross/x markers of the same colour).
Colour coding by temperature is red for 293K, orange for 373K, light green for 473K, green for 573K, cyan for 673K, blue for 773K and purple for 873K, in both panels.

In panel (a) the flow stress decreases monotonically with increasing temperature: the 293K curve rises steeply to just below the 1.4 GPa gridline at strain 0.5, whereas the 873K curve flattens at roughly 0.45 GPa over the same strain interval.

In panel (a) experimental markers follow the simulated lines closely at 293K, 373K, 473K and 573K, with visible separation at 673K and 773K where the experimental markers lie above the simulated line at higher strains.
In panel (b) the strain-hardening rate starts at approximately 3.0–3.6 GPa at the lowest strains for all temperatures and then decreases with straining.
In panel (b) the 293K curve shows a local maximum (hump) near strain 0.2–0.25 at about 2.5 GPa, and the corresponding red experimental markers exceed 2.5 GPa around strain 0.2.
In panel (b) the 873K curve decays fastest, falling close to zero hardening by strain ~0.4, showing that higher temperature suppresses strain hardening.
The caption states that the curves are for a Fe-22wt.% Mn-0.6wt.% C model TWIP steel at seven different temperatures and that one coherent parameter set was used for the whole temperature range.
The caption states the data are taken from Ref. 50 (Color figure online).

The caption describes (a) as true stress–strain compression curves and (b) as the corresponding strain-hardening curves; note the caption text for (b) refers to 'Fig. 1a' rather than Fig. 7a, an apparent typographical inconsistency with the panels as labelled.

The citing text asserts that the figure illustrates both experimental and simulated flow curves of a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C TWIP model alloy at different deformation conditions, providing evidence that a single parameter set is robust over a wide temperature range.
The citing text states that Fig. 7a shows the flow curves for a set of seven different temperatures and Fig. 7b the strain-hardening curves corresponding to the stress–strain curves of Fig. 7a.
